verdict.rationale: Bitwarden calls itself an open source password manager, and community comments back this up: one user picks it specifically because its clients are not closed source, and another notes it relicensed back to a Free/Open license after the SDK controversy. The pack has no first-party documentation of the client app repositories, their licenses, or how the TOTP/seed-handling code can be inspected, so full coverage is not shown. missing for 10: first-party docs naming the client app source repos and licenses, evidence that the seed/TOTP-handling code (e.g. the Authenticator and SDK) is public, and independent audit or community-review evidence.

support.subject: As a security engineer, the client apps are open source, so the code handling my seeds can be inspected and community-reviewed

citations.quote: The most trusted open source password manager for passwords, passkeys, and secrets
I use BitWarden because I'd never trust a password manager with closed source clients
Thank you to Bitwarden for relicensing back to Free/Open License
